--- title: "Simulation Based Estimation of Sampling Bias" jupyter: python3 fig-dpi: 300 bibliography: ../paper/references.bib --- ```{=html} ``` # Data and models **Field.** GLORYS12V1 reanalysis on its native $1/12^\circ$ grid. OHC is the $0$–$2000$ m depth integral of potential temperature against constant $c_p\rho$ (`code/ohc.py`), evaluated daily over 2010–2019. Cells enter the analysis only where $\mathrm{deptho} > 2000$ m *and* the integral is defined at every level. **Mean field.** OHC is split as $\mathrm{OHC} = \hat m + \tilde Z$ into a smooth climatological mean field $\hat m$, fitted once across $1995$–$2019$, and the residual anomaly field $\tilde Z$. $\hat m$ is a per-cell OLS on a quadratic trend plus annual and semiannual harmonics, fit against the GLORYS *monthly* record with each basis function averaged over its month to match the monthly-mean response, then evaluated pointwise per day. @sec-meanfield gives the estimator and summarizes what it leaves. **Advection.** OceanParcels, park depth $1000$ m, advected by GLORYS daily $(u,v)$ over $11$–$66^\circ$ N, $87$–$12^\circ$ W -- the full 2010-2019 footprint of every float that profiles an analysis box in 2015-2019, so simulated floats are not deleted for leaving the velocity domain (an earlier $15$–$50^\circ$ N, $70$–$30^\circ$ W domain lost most such floats at its western edge; see @sec-retention). Floats advect continuously at park depth and record a position every $10$ days; there is no ascent, descent or surface drift, so a cycle is a position sample, not a simulated dive. Floats are deleted on leaving the velocity domain and retired at a lifespan drawn from the real Argo record for this region (median $\approx 1500$ d). **Estimation.** $\hat Z_k$ is the unweighted mean of $\tilde Z_k$ at the profile positions for year $k$, and $\bar Z_k$ is the exact $\mathbb{P}$-weighted domain mean of the same field for year $k$. # The analysis domain Two analysis boxes sit inside the downloaded GLORYS region, both spanning $60^\circ$–$40^\circ$ W: **Box B** ($35$–$45^\circ$ N) straddles the North Atlantic Current and the Gulf Stream extension, and **Box A** ($22$–$34^\circ$ N) has milder currents and OHC variability. Temperature was downloaded for the analysis boxes and a small buffer; velocity was downloaded over a larger region to advect floats, which are lost if they exit the velocity domain. ::: {#cell-fig-domain .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The two analysis boxes (filled) inside the downloaded GLORYS velocity and thetao regions (dashed).](osim_files/figure-html/fig-domain-output-1.png){#fig-domain width=837 height=622} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-bathy .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![GLORYS ocean depth over the advection domain (left) and the sub-2000 m cells excluded from the analysis (right), both boxes outlined.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-bathy-output-1.png){#fig-bathy width=1402 height=564} ::: ::: An analysis mask is placed on cells that must have temperature data for every depth level to $2000$m. Retained area is $92.35\%$ and $99.77\%$ for Box B and A respectively. The below figures show a single day's OHC anomaly and velocity fields for the analysis domain. A day was selected based on its percentile of spatial variability across cells for the given field over both analysis boxes. ::: {#cell-fig-days .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Residual field Z (GJ per m2) on days at the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile of the combined daily spatial dispersion, both boxes on one shared diverging scale.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-days-output-1.png){#fig-days width=1403 height=535} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-vel-u .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Eastward velocity at 1000 m (cm/s), both boxes on one shared diverging scale.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-vel-u-output-1.png){#fig-vel-u width=1403 height=535} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-vel-v .cell execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Northward velocity at 1000 m (cm/s), both boxes on one shared diverging scale.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-vel-v-output-1.png){#fig-vel-v width=1403 height=535} ::: ::: **The flow is roughly twice as variable in Box B.** Median daily $\mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}$ is $12.1$ cm/s eastward and $11.5$ northward in Box B against $5.5$ and $5.4$ in Box A. Over 2010-2019, the range of daily spatial standard deviation in cm/s is $9.7$–$14.8$ (eastward) and $9.0$–$14.7$ (northward) in Box B, $4.5$–$7.0$ (eastward) and $4.4$–$6.7$ (northward) in Box A. # Mean field {#sec-meanfield} The sampling-bias question concerns the *residual anomaly* OHC field, not the total. We therefore decompose $$\mathrm{OHC}(c,t) \;=\; \hat m(c,t) \;+\; \tilde Z(c,t),$$ with $\hat m$ a mean field fitted per cell once across all years and $\tilde Z_k$ the year-$k$ residual the designs sample. **Regression.** For each analysis cell $c$, OHC is modelled as $\mathrm{OHC}(c,t) = \phi(t)^\top \beta_c + \varepsilon(c,t)$ on the trend-plus-harmonics basis $\phi(t) = \bigl(1,\,t,\,t^2,\,\sin 2\pi t,\,\cos 2\pi t,\,\sin 4\pi t,\,\cos 4\pi t\bigr)^\top$ ($t$ in decimal years): a quadratic trend and the annual and semiannual cycles. The coefficients are fit by least squares to the $1995$–$2019$ GLORYS *monthly* mean record. A GLORYS monthly file holds the month *mean* OHC over $I_m = [t_0^m, t_1^m)$ but is time-stamped at its start $t_0^m$. So we regress on the **window-averaged basis** $\bar\phi(I_m) = |I_m|^{-1}\!\int_{I_m}\phi(t)\,dt$, so the OHC monthly response and seasonal basis are monthly averages. The design matrix is $\bar X = \bigl[\bar\phi(I_m)^\top\bigr]_m$ and the per-cell fit is $\hat\beta_c = \bar X^{+} Y_c$. **Prediction is then pointwise:** the fitted field is evaluated at each instant on the daily grid, $\hat m(c,t) = \phi(t)^\top \hat\beta_c$, and subtracted from daily OHC to give $\tilde Z_k = \mathrm{OHC}_k - \hat m$ on the same mask. ::: {#cell-fig-meanfield .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Fitted mean field (quadratic trend plus annual and semiannual harmonics) at mid-month 2015, both boxes on one shared scale, in GJ per m2.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-meanfield-output-1.png){#fig-meanfield width=1484 height=474} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-decomp3 .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The OHC = mean field + residual decomposition on one shared day, both boxes drawn per field, in GJ per m2.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-decomp3-output-1.png){#fig-decomp3 width=1469 height=681} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-ohc-series .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Daily domain-mean OHC with the fitted mean field (top) and their difference, the domain-mean anomaly (bottom), per box over 2010-2019 in GJ per m2.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-ohc-series-output-1.png){#fig-ohc-series width=1199 height=704} ::: ::: # Estimand, truth, and estimator Let $\mathbb{P}$ be the normalized area $\times$ time probability measure over the depth masked analysis domain. The target is the residual field's domain mean, $$\bar Z_k \;=\; \int_{\mathcal{X}} \tilde Z_k \, d\mathbb{P},$$ for each analysis year $k$, where $\tilde Z_k$ is the year-$k$ OHC 0–2000 m field with the fitted mean field removed. A design is a finite point set $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^{n} \subset \mathcal{X}$ — the year-$k$ in-box profiles of one deployment realization $d$; its estimator and bias are $$\hat Z^{(d)}_k \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \tilde Z_k\!\left(x_i^{(d)}\right), \qquad B^{(d)}_k \;=\; \hat Z^{(d)}_k - \bar Z_k .$$ $\tilde Z_k$ is a simple function on the native $1/12^\circ \times$ daily grid, so evaluating it at $x_i$ is the cell-day lookup of the *containing* cell. ::: {#e6dec302 .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}

The dispersion $\sigma_k = \mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k)$ is $6.3$–$7.6$ GJ/m$^2$ in Box B and $1.7$–$2.4$ in Box A. # Deployment One continuous advection per realization generates the sampling. For realization $d$, $N$ floats are seeded uniformly over normalized spacetime across the velocity record of 2010-2019. Each realization therefore yields $B^{(d)}_k$ for every analysis year at once, flow and field the same calendar year. **How a float is advected.** Each float is carried by GLORYS12V1 daily horizontal velocity $(u,v)$ at a fixed park depth of $1000$ m and held there for its whole life — there is *no dive cycle*. The two archived velocity levels bracketing $1000$ m ($902$ and $1062$ m) are linearly interpolated to the park depth (as OceanParcels does natively), and the float is stepped forward at a $1$-hour time step. Its position is written every $10$ days, and that recorded park-depth position is taken as the profile — the point where a real float would begin its ascent — so a cycle is a position sample, not a simulated dive. A float is deleted when it leaves the velocity domain and retired at a lifespan drawn from the real Argo record (median $\approx 1500$ d). ::: {.callout-note} This version reflects the **expanded velocity domain** ($11$–$66^\circ$ N, $87$–$12^\circ$ W). The pilot below is a **preliminary $16$-realization re-run** on that domain (the full $100$-rep run is pending); its confidence intervals are correspondingly wider. The argo-actual comparison arm (@sec-argo-cmp) is on the new domain; the resampled argo-bootstrap ensemble has been removed pending its re-run. ::: The pilot is **$16$ independent realizations** (preliminary; target $100$). Each seeds **$1{,}000$ floats** uniformly over normalized space–time on the ($\mathrm{deptho}\ge 1000$ m) region spanning both boxes plus an $8^\circ$ margin, across $2010\text{-}01\text{-}01$ to $2019\text{-}12\text{-}26$, and advects them once at $1000$ m park depth ($10$-day profiling cycle, lifespans drawn from the real Argo record). Years $2010$–$2014$ are the equilibration lead; bias is calculated on **$2015$–$2019$**. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Simulated advection ::: {#cell-fig-advection .cell execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![One simulated deployment: 60 float drift tracks and their 10-day profile points coloured by year, only in-box profiles (filled) entering an estimate.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-advection-output-1.png){#fig-advection width=947 height=648} ::: ::: ### Real Argo ::: {#cell-fig-advection-argo .cell execution_count=13} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Real Argo trajectories over the same domain and years (60 of 740 floats) coloured by year, on the same base map for comparison.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-advection-argo-output-1.png){#fig-advection-argo width=947 height=648} ::: ::: ::: **Real deployment geometry.** The map below shows the raw (not QC-cleaned) deployment position of every real Argo float first observed inside the advection domain over $2010$–$2019$ ($1{,}014$ floats), coloured by deployment year — the release geometry the real-deployment arms (below) seed from, and the starting point for the per-float bias-over-time analysis. Deployment is taken as each float's earliest profile on record, so a float first observed before the file window is not resolved here. ::: {#cell-fig-deploy-positions .cell execution_count=14} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Raw Argo deployment positions in the advection domain, 2010-2019, coloured by deployment year, on the shared domain base map (dashed: velocity and thetao download regions; filled: the two analysis boxes).](osim_files/figure-html/fig-deploy-positions-output-1.png){#fig-deploy-positions width=947 height=648} ::: ::: ## A single deployment cluster {#sec-cluster} Six floats were deployed within a $\sim\!14$-hour window on $27$–$28$ September $2015$ in a tight cluster in the NW corner of Box B ($43.4$–$44.3^\circ$ N, $-55.8$ to $-57.8^\circ$ W), on the Grand Banks / Gulf Stream–Labrador confluence. They are a clean natural experiment in deployment geometry: a common release point and time, whose per-float sampling bias we can then follow profile by profile. For the simple-mean estimator the year-$k$ bias is an *exact* sum of per-profile contributions. Writing $n_k$ for the number of in-box profiles the array reports in year $k$, $$ B_k \;=\; \hat Z_k - \bar Z_k \;=\; \frac{1}{n_k}\sum_{i=1}^{n_k}\bigl(\tilde Z_k(x_i) - \bar Z_k\bigr) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{n_k} c_i, \qquad c_i \;=\; \frac{1}{n_k}\,\underbrace{\bigl(\tilde Z_k(x_i) - \bar Z_k\bigr)}_{\delta_i}, $$ the centering being free because $\tfrac{1}{n_k}\sum_i \bar Z_k = \bar Z_k$. Every profile carries the *same* weight $1/n_k$ whatever float it came from — that equal weighting is what makes the estimator the simple (unweighted) mean, and it ties the normalization to the year, not the float. Grouping the contributions by float gives each float's share of the year's bias, $$ C_{f,k} \;=\; \sum_{i\,\in\, f,\,k} c_i \;=\; \frac{n_{f,k}}{n_k}\bigl(\bar Z_{f,k} - \bar Z_k\bigr), \qquad \sum_f C_{f,k} = B_k, $$ its profile share $n_{f,k}/n_k$ times its mean alignment $\bar Z_{f,k} - \bar Z_k$ (with $\bar Z_{f,k}$ the mean of $\tilde Z_k$ over that float's year-$k$ in-box profiles). The charts below plot the single-profile bias $\delta_i = \tilde Z_k(x_i) - \bar Z_k$ — one profile's alignment with the field — along each float's life (in-box profiles only, where the residual field is defined), with the cluster mean over-plotted. This is the contribution $c_i$ up to the $1/n_k$ weight; we show $\delta_i$ rather than $c_i$ so the curves stay comparable across years (the year's $n_k$ only rescales them). The two tabs evaluate $\delta_i$ at the *real* Argo positions and at the *GLORYS park-advection* sim-twin positions of the same floats, so their divergence is the same real-vs-reanalysis gap the trajectory maps show. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Real Argo ::: {#cell-fig-cluster-bias .cell execution_count=15} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Single-profile bias Z(x_i) - Zbar_k (GJ per m2) vs profile number for each of the six floats at their real Argo positions, with the cluster mean (black). Only in-box profiles carry a defined bias.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-cluster-bias-output-1.png){#fig-cluster-bias width=1198 height=539} ::: ::: ### GLORYS advection ::: {#cell-fig-cluster-bias-sim .cell execution_count=16} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The same single-profile bias evaluated at the GLORYS 1000 m park-advection sim-twin positions of the six floats. In-box counts differ from the real tab because the park tracks drift out of the box on a different schedule.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-cluster-bias-sim-output-1.png){#fig-cluster-bias-sim width=1198 height=539} ::: ::: ::: The two trajectory maps below trace the same six floats (one colour each; deployment a star, last fix an open circle): the GLORYS park-advection sim twin against the real Argo path from the shared deployment. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### GLORYS advection ::: {#cell-fig-cluster-sim .cell execution_count=17} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![GLORYS 1000 m park-advection sim-twin trajectories of the six floats from their real deployment positions.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-cluster-sim-output-1.png){#fig-cluster-sim width=947 height=727} ::: ::: ### Real Argo ::: {#cell-fig-cluster-real .cell execution_count=18} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Real Argo trajectories of the same six floats on the same base map.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-cluster-real-output-1.png){#fig-cluster-real width=947 height=727} ::: ::: ::: ## Domain retention {#sec-retention} The expanded velocity domain almost eliminates the loss of floats to advection out of bounds. The table and map below classify the fate of every virtual float in the **argo-actual arm** ($365$ floats seeded from real deployments, advected once over $2010$–$2019$ on the new domain): each either leaves the velocity domain early (deleted), retires at its drawn lifespan, or is still alive at the record end. Only **$3.6\%$** ($13/365$) exit the domain, and $12$ of those $13$ leave at the *southern* edge ($\sim\!11^\circ$ N) -- the western edge that flushed floats on the old domain is now deep interior. (This is the single-realization argo-actual arm; a per-realization count for the uniform pilot needs its full trajectories, which the pilot run discards, so it is deferred to an instrumented re-run.) ::: {#79348654 .cell execution_count=19} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=18} ```{=html}

Almost all exits are at the southern boundary.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-domain-exit-output-1.png){#fig-domain-exit width=947 height=727} ::: ::: # The sampling weight field The bias $B^{(d)}_k = \langle \tilde Z_k,\, w^{(d)} - p\rangle$, the inner product of the residual field with the excess of the empirical sampling weight over the uniform weight p. One realization's sampling is the normalized empirical measure $$w^{(d)} \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \delta_{x_i}$$ on the spacetime domain $\mathcal{X} = \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{T}$. Averaging it over realizations gives $\mathbb{E}[w]$, the normalized occupancy (intensity) measure of the advective array, with $\mathbb{E}[B_k] = \langle \tilde Z_k,\, \mathbb{E}[w] - p\rangle$. We define the spatial marginal sampling weight as $$w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} w_{c,\tau} \;=\; \frac{\#\{\,i : x_i \in c\,\}}{n},$$ the fraction of a realization's profiles that fall in cell $c$, summed over all days. The maps below show $\mathbb{E}[w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c]$ — the expected such fraction, i.e. the array's normalized spatial intensity — over the years $2015$–$2019$ on the native $1/12^\circ$ grid, against the uniform area marginal $p^{\mathrm{sp}}_c = A_c / \sum_{c'} A_{c'}$, as the ratio $q_c = \mathbb{E}[w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c] / p^{\mathrm{sp}}_c$ ($=1$ under area-fair sampling). ## Spatial marginal ::: {#cell-fig-wspace .cell execution_count=21} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Over- and under-sampling log2(E[w]/uniform) on the native 1/12 deg grid, both boxes on one map per scored year and one shared scale (red over-sampled, blue under, white uniform).](osim_files/figure-html/fig-wspace-output-1.png){#fig-wspace width=1692 height=431} ::: ::: The per-cell weight distribution about the uniform value of 1, one panel per year: ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Box B ::: {#cell-fig-whist .cell execution_count=22} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box B distribution of the per-cell weight E[w]/uniform over native cells per year, about the uniform value of 1 (red line).](osim_files/figure-html/fig-whist-output-1.png){#fig-whist width=1417 height=318} ::: ::: ### Box A ::: {#cell-fig-whist-a .cell execution_count=23} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box A distribution of the per-cell weight E[w]/uniform, same construction as Box B.](osim_files/figure-html/fig-whist-a-output-1.png){#fig-whist-a width=1417 height=318} ::: ::: ::: ## Bias as a covariance Let $q = w/p$ be the sampling frequency of each cell-day relative to its uniform share — the over/under-sampling factor mapped in @fig-wspace and distributed in @fig-whist, equal to $1$ under uniform sampling and with $\int q\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P} = 1$. The bias is the inner product of the field with the sampling excess, $$B_k \;=\; \langle \tilde Z_k,\, q - 1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}} \;=\; \langle \tilde Z_k - \bar Z_k,\, q - 1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}},$$ the second equality because $\langle 1, q-1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}} = 0$ — a spatially uniform field is sampled without bias. Cauchy–Schwarz for this inner product gives the cap $$|B_k| \;\le\; \lVert \tilde Z_k - \bar Z_k\rVert_{\mathbb{P}}\,\lVert q - 1\rVert_{\mathbb{P}} \;=\; \sigma_k \, \operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q),$$ with $\sigma_k = \operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k)$ (the residual-field table) and $\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q)$ the spread of the over/under-sampling factor (@fig-whist), attained only when $q-1$ is proportional to the field anomaly. **Zero bias does not require uniform sampling** — it requires only that $q - 1$ be orthogonal to $\tilde Z_k$ in $L^2(\mathbb{P})$; a strongly non-uniform array ($\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q) \gg 0$) can still be unbiased for this functional. # Results ## Pilot specification Across the $16$ realizations the pilot seeds $1.6\times10^4$ float-deployments; per-box, per-year sample sizes are in the table below. On the expanded domain Box B retains slightly more floats than before (standing stock $\sim\!45$–$48$, $\sim\!1{,}640$–$1{,}750$ profiles a year); Box A holds stock $\sim\!75$–$80$ giving $\sim\!2{,}720$–$2{,}910$ — its quiescent flow retains more of the same deployment. ::: {#9751d6ea .cell execution_count=25} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=24} ```{=html}

missing dive cycle? The park-only sim omits the dive cycle — the ascent, the $\sim\!1$-day surface drift, and the descent — so one reading of the residual $\sim\!0.3$ GJ/m$^2$ is that a profile recorded at the $1000$ m park position sits systematically away from where a real float actually surfaces. Each float is a matched colour pair -- real the darker solid line, sim twin the lighter dashed line: a Box A float in blue/cyan (~8 yr, subtropical gyre) and a Box B float in purple/pink (~6 yr, NAC / Gulf Stream).](osim_files/figure-html/fig-twins-output-1.png){#fig-twins width=947 height=704} ::: ::: The sim loses the real float fast: median separation is already $\sim\!53$ km at one $10$-day cycle, $\sim\!135$ km at a month and $\sim\!290$ km at three, climbing through $\sim\!590$ km at a year (@fig-divergence). The field's mesoscale correlation length is $\sim\!50$–$100$ km, so the GLORYS-park position exceeds it *within a single cycle* and is several correlation lengths off well inside the analysis year — it samples effectively independent locations at the seasonal scale that sets the bias. Individual twins make this concrete (@fig-twins): a subtropical-gyre float and its twin part slowly, while a NAC / Gulf-Stream float and its twin split early and end up in different parts of the basin. A dive cycle would add only the $\sim\!1$-day surface excursion per cycle (tens of km, largely non-persistent), far too small to produce or repair a divergence that grows at $\sim\!5$ km/day. **So the drift residual is reanalysis and advection error — real $1000$ m currents and unresolved eddies, not the missing surfacing — and adding a dive cycle to the advection would not close it.** (The $\pm 6$-day matching tolerance inflates the $10$-day point; the month-plus separations dwarf it, and the separation also bundles the surface-vs-park offset, which only reinforces the conclusion.) # Conclusions From this $100$-realization pilot: **The advective sampling bias is small but not zero.** In both boxes $\mathbb{E}[B_k]$ stays within $\sim\!0.02\,\sigma_k$ (the bias tables) — a few hundredths of a GJ/m$^2$ against a field varying by $6$–$8$ (Box B) and $2$ (Box A) GJ/m$^2$. It is not identically zero: several years are resolved at $2$–$4$ Monte-Carlo standard errors, so the array is weakly preferential in effect, at a magnitude that is a small fraction of the field's own variability. **Strong non-uniform sampling, nearly orthogonal to the field.** The array samples space genuinely non-uniformly (on-mask up to $\sim\!3.6\times$ over-sampling, $\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q)\approx0.4$; @fig-whist), yet the bias is only $\sim\!1$–$5\%$ of the Cauchy–Schwarz ceiling that non-uniformity permits, i.e. a weight–field correlation $|\rho_k|\approx0.02$. Preferential sampling does not imply preferential bias for this functional — the estimand-level bias is the covariance $\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathbb{P}}(q,\tilde Z_k)$, and the array sits near its null space, not a property of sampling non-uniformity per se. **Both regimes are comparably biased once standardized.** Box B has larger raw bias and spread, but on the $\sigma_k$ scale the energetic western-boundary region is not disproportionately biased relative to the quiescent gyre.
